arxiv-2203-11069.title: Model BOSS & eBOSS Luminous Red Galaxies at 0.2 < z < 1.0 0.2<z<1.0 using SubHalo Abundance Matching with 3 parameters Model BOSS & eBOSS Luminous Red Galaxies at 0.2 < z < 1.0 0.2<z<1.0 using SubHalo Abundance Matching with 3 parameters – 25
arxiv-2203-11069.creator: Jiaxi Yu, Cheng Zhao, Chia-Hsun Chuang, Julian E. Bautista, Ginevra Favole, Jean-Paul Kneib, Faizan G. Mohammad, Ashley J. Ross, Anand Raichoor, Charling Tao, Kyle Dawson, Graziano Rossi
arxiv-2203-11069.description: Abstract SubHalo Abundance Matching (SHAM) is an empirical method for constructing galaxy catalogues based on high-resolution N N -body simulations. We apply SHAM on the UNIT simulation to simulate SDSS BOSS/eBOSS Luminous Red Galaxies (LRGs) within a wide redshift range of 0.2 < z < 1.0 0.2<z<1.0 .

arxiv-2207-12222.title: Inviscid limit for the compressible Navier-Stokes equations with density dependent viscosity
arxiv-2207-12222.creator: Luca Bisconti Matteo Caggio 1. Università degli Studi di Firenze Dipartimento di Matematica e Informatica “U. Dini”Viale Morgagni 67/a, I-50134 Firenze, Italia2. Institute of Mathematics of the Academy of Sciences of the Czech Republic,Žitná 25, 11567, Praha 1, Czech Republic* corresponding author:
arxiv-2207-12222.description: Abstract We consider the compressible Navier-Stokes system describing the motion of a barotropic fluid with density dependent viscosity confined in a three-dimensional bounded domain Ω \Omega . We show the convergence of the weak solution to the compressible Navier-Stokes system to the strong solution to the compressible Euler system when the viscosity and the damping coefficients tend to zero.

arxiv-2211-12681.title: Benchmarking Adversarially Robust Quantum Machine Learning at Scale
arxiv-2211-12681.creator: Maxwell T. West, Sarah M. Erfani, Christopher Leckie, Martin Sevior, Lloyd C.L. Hollenberg, Muhammad Usman
arxiv-2211-12681.description: Abstract Machine learning (ML) methods such as artificial neural networks are rapidly becoming ubiquitous in modern science, technology and industry. Despite their accuracy and sophistication, neural networks can be easily fooled by carefully designed malicious inputs known as adversarial attacks.

arxiv-2301-06831.title: Generalizing Impermanent Loss on Decentralized Exchanges with Constant Function Market Makers
arxiv-2301-06831.creator: Rohan Tangri, Peter Yatsyshin, Elisabeth A. Duijnstee, Danilo Mandic
arxiv-2301-06831.description: Abstract Liquidity providers are essential for the function of decentralized exchanges to ensure liquidity takers can be guaranteed a counterparty for their trades. However, liquidity providers investing in liquidity pools face many risks, the most prominent of which is impermanent loss.

arxiv-2402-14818.title: Palo : A Polyglot Large Multimodal Model for 5B People
arxiv-2402-14818.creator: Muhammad Maaz, Hanoona Rasheed, Abdelrahman Shaker, Salman Khan, Hisham Cholakal, Rao M. Anwer, Tim Baldwin, Michael Felsberg, Fahad S. Khan, [0.25cm] Mohamed bin Zayed University of AI, Australian National University, Aalto University, The University of Melbourne, Linköping University
arxiv-2402-14818.description: Abstract In pursuit of more inclusive Vision-Language Models (VLMs), this study introduces a Large Multilingual Multimodal Model called Palo . Palo offers visual reasoning capabilities in 10 major languages, including English, Chinese, Hindi, Spanish, French, Arabic, Bengali, Russian, Urdu, and Japanese, that span a total of ∼ \sim 5B people (65% of the world population).

arxiv-2404-00044.title: UAlign: Pushing the Limit of Template-free Retrosynthesis Prediction with Unsupervised SMILES Alignment
arxiv-2404-00044.creator: Kaipeng Zeng, Bo Yang, Xin Zhao, Yu Zhang, Fan Nie, Xiaokang Yang, Yaohui Jin, Yanyan Xu
arxiv-2404-00044.description: Abstract Motivation Retrosynthesis planning poses a formidable challenge in the organic chemical industry, particularly in pharmaceuticals. Single-step retrosynthesis prediction, a crucial step in the planning process, has witnessed a surge in interest in recent years due to advancements in AI for science.

arxiv-2411-07393.title: Monitoring of DDO68 ’Northern Ring’ SF regions during years 2016–2023
arxiv-2411-07393.creator: S.A. Pustilnik, Y.A. Perepelitsyna, A.S. Vinokurov, E.S. Egorova, A.S. Moskvitin, V.P. Goranskij, A.N. Burenkov, O.A. Maslennikova, O.I. Spiridonova
arxiv-2411-07393.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by S.A. Pustilnik, Y.A. Perepelitsyna, A.S. Vinokurov, E.S. Egorova, A.S. Moskvitin, V.P. Goranskij, A.N. Burenkov, O.A. Maslennikova, O.I. Spiridonova. DDO68 is a star-forming (SF) dwarf galaxy residing in a nearby void. Its gas metallicity is among the lowest known in the local Universe, with parameter 12+log(O/H) in the range of 6.96–7.3 dex. Six of its SF regions are located in or near the so-called ’Northern Ring’, in which the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) images reveal many luminous young stars.

arxiv-2509-04992.title: Improving Spatial Resolution of Background Oriented Schlieren Based on Directional Rays
arxiv-2509-04992.creator: Xiang Li, Muen Gao, Weiran Wang, Jiawei Li, Chong Pan, Jinjun Wang, Yuan Xiong
arxiv-2509-04992.description: Abstract The background-oriented Schlieren technique has emerged as a promising method for visualizing density gradients and performing quantitative measurements. However, an inherent constraint of BOS is the compromise between spatial resolution and measurement sensitivity, as the BOS camera typically remains focused on the background pattern.

Our network achieves an AUC of 0.895 in predicting the presence of cancer in the breast, when tested on the...

pmc-11326710.title: A quantitative description of light-limited cyanobacterial growth using flux balance analysis
pmc-11326710.creator: Rune Höper, Daria Komkova, Tomáš Zavřel, Ralf Steuer, Mark Alber, Christoph Kaleta, Christoph Kaleta, Christoph Kaleta, Christoph Kaleta
pmc-11326710.description: The metabolism of phototrophic cyanobacteria is an integral part of global biogeochemical cycles, and the capability of cyanobacteria to assimilate atmospheric CO2 into organic carbon has manifold potential applications for a sustainable biotechnology. To elucidate the properties of cyanobacterial metabolism and growth, computational reconstructions of genome-scale metabolic networks play an increasingly important role.

pmc-11646786.title: Impact of extreme temperature on congenital heart disease mortality: a population-based nationwide case-crossover study
pmc-11646786.creator: Qiyu He, Xinyue Lang, Huayan Shen, Jiangmei Liu, Sirui Zhou, Jing Wei, Xinjie Lin, Yuze Liu, Kai Ma, Zheng Dou, Zhou Zhou, Maigeng Zhou, Shoujun Li
pmc-11646786.description: SummaryBackgroundThe association between congenital heart disease (CHD) and non-optimal temperatures has received limited investigation. We aimed to investigate the impact of extreme temperatures on CHD mortality.MethodsWe reviewed the National Mortality Surveillance System of China and retrieved death records attributable to CHD from 2013 to 2021.

pmc-12395755.title: State-of-the-art preclinical techniques to study the impact of spreading depolarizations in awake rodents
pmc-12395755.creator: Alejandro Labastida-Ramirez, Neela K. Codadu, Kagan Agan, Robert C. Wykes
pmc-12395755.description: BackgroundUnderstanding the mechanisms of pathological brain network activity and the efficacy of therapies requires testing hypothesis in vivo, where brain circuitry remains preserved. Therefore, animal models are a key tool in the study of primary neurological disorders such as migraine, stroke and epilepsy.

pmc-12597870.title: Physician assistant legalization and conflicts in South Korea: need for an approach based on lessons from three countries
pmc-12597870.creator: Suhyun Oh, Kye-Hyun Kim, Seog-Kyun Mun
pmc-12597870.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ide essential medical services at large hospitals, raising fundamental questions about medical personnel management’s efficiency and sustainability. Discussions on the physician assistant (PA) system and its legalization to fill medical care gaps caused by residents’ absence are gaining momentum. As of 2022, the number of doctors in Korea is about 140 000 [1] and the number of PA is about 6000 [2].

pmc-13191587.title: Improving catalytic aquathermolysis of heavy oil using a tri-metal supported zeolite catalyst
pmc-13191587.creator: Yifeng Sun, Shengke Li, Chuanmin Xiao, Qicheng Liu, Ding Wei, Jiang Yang
pmc-13191587.description: A hierarchical zeolite-supported trimetallic catalyst (Mo/Co/Ni-ZSM-5) was synthesized via incipient wetness impregnation and evaluated for the hydrothermal upgrading of heavy oil. The catalytic system was designed to integrate acidic cracking functionality with metal-mediated hydrogenation under aquathermolysis conditions. Mono- and bimetallic counterparts were investigated for comparison. Among all tested catalysts, Mo/Co/Ni-ZSM-5 exhibited the highest hydrogenation activity and viscosity-reduction efficiency.

pmc-13266207.title: Comparative analysis of Antigliotic Guiding Regenerative Gel (AGRG - LDP-916) for peripheral nerve reconstruction: Evidence from prospective randomized controlled studies
pmc-13266207.creator: S Rochkind, A Goldlust, M Almog
pmc-13266207.description: IntroductionPeripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) with segmental defects remain a challenge. Autologous nerve grafts (ANG) are the gold standard but are limited by donor-site morbidity and variable outcomes in long-gap repairs. Processed allografts and synthetic conduits provide alternatives but lack biological cues for optimal regeneration.

pmc-13403226.title: Measurements of Liquid Ammonia Sprays Using the ECN Spray M Injector with Injector-To-Injector Comparisons
pmc-13403226.creator: Li Shen, Abdullah U. Bajwa, Felix Leach
pmc-13403226.description: Liquid ammonia is receiving increasing attention as a carbon-free energy carrier for use in internal combustion engines, particularly in the maritime sector. While gaseous ammonia injection has been widely studied, liquid-phase injection offers potential advantages in terms of fuel–air mixing and power density, but introduces challenges associated with evaporation, flash boiling, and spray collapse.

pmc-13524734.title: Pilot randomized controlled trial of a peer coach-led behavioral and educational intervention to enhance quality of life in patients living with hypersensitivity pneumonitis: Protocol for the RISE-HP study
pmc-13524734.creator: CM Zhang, K Chau, S Banerjee, JJ Swigris, JK Krishnan, RJ Kaner, FJ Martinez, JN Tobin, MM Safford, KI Aronson
pmc-13524734.description: BackgroundHypersensitivity Pneumonitis (HP) is an interstitial lung disease caused by an inhalational environmental exposure. Patients living with HP experience significant stress, uncertainty, and hypervigilance about the management of their disease and prognosis. These factors lead to reduced health-related quality of life (HRQOL), an important outcome that no interventions currently target.

pmc-13560950.title: The Significant Impact of the Evolution of Porous Architecture in Sol–Gel Processed-Nanoscale ZnO-Bearing Bioactive Glass in a Physiological Environment
pmc-13560950.creator: Mahesh Malpani, Saikat Chattopadhyay, Raja Devesh Kumar Misra, Kamakhya Prakash Misra
pmc-13560950.description: IntroductionThe incorporation of network stabilizer trace elements such as zinc in bioactive glass is an effective strategy to enhance biological response and modulate degradation kinetics. However, the quantitative relation among ZnO concentration, lattice micro-strain, and evolution of dynamic pore during in vitro mineralization remains unclear.

pmc-13642151.title: Polarization‐ and Frequency‐Selective Light Amplification in Magneto‐Optic Photonic Time Crystals
pmc-13642151.creator: Shuqiao Xu, Haoshuang Zhong, Zicheng Yang, Guoyong Zhang, Hao Chen, Xiao Chen, Bo Chu, Zhuo Chen, Zhenlin Wang
pmc-13642151.description: Light amplification in photonic time crystals (PTCs), enabled by their momentum bandgap, is a well‐established phenomenon. However, prior research has predominantly focused on achieving a substantial gap, whereas the controlled manipulation of light properties remains largely unexplored. Here, we exploit spatially finite magneto‐optic photonic time crystals (MO‐PTCs) to achieve polarization‐ and frequency‐selective light amplification.
